description:
LEAF spun out of task-f4f45c281ab64f6dbf2c4ff163140010 (remote deploy cannot deliver environment variables) by architect-ed42e60a, 2026-09-09. That row is the CONSUMER and declares this row in its dependsOn. Filed separately because the consumer's blast radius was measured at 12 files, over the plan cap.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Remote delivery needs the plaintext to reach the container without ever naming a path on the docker host, because a bind mount's source is resolved on the DOCKER host and for sshTarget !== null that is not the daemon's machine. The measured shape is `docker create` + `docker cp -` (a USTAR archive on stdin) + `docker start`: the bytes go host memory -> docker CLI stdin -> container filesystem, and it works identically local and remote because the runner already carries stdin through `ssh <target> docker ...`.

- deploy-service.ts:190-192 already threads stdin through the one `run(target, args, stdin?)` seam for both local and ssh.
- `runCandidateArgv` (deploy-candidate-environment.ts:93-100) is the only builder of the candidate's start argv; `startCandidate` at deploy-service.ts:226-232 is the only caller.
- The docker double's dispatch is deploy-ports.ts:338-370, `if (verb === "run")` at :346 (the parent description said :341 - drift, re-measure).
- `tests/e2e/control-room/fake-docker-dependencies.ts:42` keys candidate health seeding on `args[0] === "run"`.
- No reusable tar writer exists in this repo. `tools/packaging/pack-source.test.ts` is the only USTAR mention and it is a reader-side assertion, not a writer.

SCOPE: BUILDERS AND DOUBLES ONLY. This row wires NOTHING into deploy-service.ts and removes NO refusal. `runCandidateArgv` stays exported and byte-identical, `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED` stays in place and still fires for sshTarget !== null, and every existing consumer of the `run` verb stays green WITHOUT EDITS. Copying to `/` with the archive carrying `run/moe/env` plus its directory entries is the shape that cannot fail on a missing destination, but confirm it against a real container before pinning it. implementationPlan.description: Teach the double `create`, `cp` and `start`, in the moved deploy-docker-double.ts. Today `dispatch` handles `run` by reading the `--name` VALUE (never the trailing argv, which is the image tag) and setting the container STARTING. Model create-then-start with the same key: `create` registers the name in a not-yet-running state, `start` moves it to STARTING, and `cp` is accepted only for a name that exists. The existing `run` path stays exactly as it is — this row wires nothing, so every current arm must keep passing untouched. Arms, each asserting the specific outcome and not merely that something happened: a container that was CREATED but never STARTED does not report itself running through `healthOf`/`inspect`; `cp` to an ABSENT container FAILS rather than succeeding silently, because a silent success is what would let a wired deploy start a candidate with no environment and blame the health probe; `cp` carries its payload on the `stdin` argument the dispatch already receives, and the double records it so a later row can assert no value reached an argv. Put these arms in deploy-candidate-environment.test.ts, which already imports `createDockerDouble` and `DOUBLE_IMAGE_COMMAND`, rather than opening a tenth file.

implementationPlan.description: The USTAR encoder, in a new apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-archive.ts plus its tracked `.js` bridge. It lives in its own module because deploy-candidate-environment.ts is already 217 lines against a 250-line target. Encode a single-file archive from the already-encoded environment text: 512-byte header, name, mode, uid, gid, size, mtime, the checksum computed over the header with the checksum field spaces-filled, typeflag, the `ustar\000` magic and version, then the data padded to a 512 multiple, then two zero blocks. THE uid AND gid FIELDS ARE NOT DECORATION — they carry the values step 1 measured for the image's app user, and getting them wrong produces a file the app cannot read. Include the directory entries the destination path needs if step 1 showed `docker cp` will not create them. Mode stays owner-only. The runner's stdin is a STRING, so the encoder must emit something that survives a UTF-8 round trip: headers are ASCII, but a variable VALUE is arbitrary text, so verify the byte length written into the size field is the UTF-8 byte length and not the JavaScript string length — a multi-byte character silently truncates the payload otherwise, and tar reports no error for a short read it was told to expect. Keep the module under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
USTAR ENCODER LANDED in a new apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-archive.ts (164 lines) plus its tracked `.js` bridge. `deploy-candidate-environment.ts` is UNCHANGED by this step and stays at 217.

SHAPE. `encodeCandidateArchive(text, path = CANDIDATE_ENVIRONMENT_PATH, mtime = 0)` returns a discriminated result — `{ok:true, archive}` or `{ok:false, code}` — matching `DeployCandidateEnvironmentResult`'s shape in the sibling module rather than inventing a second convention. Emits: the parent directory header (0755, typeflag 5), the file header (0600, typeflag 0), the payload, NUL padding to the next 512 boundary, then two zero blocks. Field offsets are the USTAR ones and were arithmetic-checked, not eyeballed: name@0/100, mode@100/8, uid@108/8, gid@116/8, size@124/12, mtime@136/12, chksum@148/8, typeflag@156/1, linkname@157/100, magic@257 `ustar\0`, version@263 `00`, uname@265/32, gname@297/32, devmajor@329/8, devminor@337/8, prefix@345/155 — summing to 500, padded to 512. Checksum is computed over the header with its own field SPACE-FILLED and written back as six octal digits, NUL, space.

FOUR DECISIONS EACH MADE BY MEASUREMENT, NOT PREFERENCE.
1. uid/gid 1000/1000 from step 1's `id -u node`/`id -g node` on the pinned image, with the counterfactual (uid 0 => `Permission denied` for the app user) as the control. Constants `ARCHIVE_OWNER_UID`/`ARCHIVE_OWNER_GID` are exported so an arm pins them.
2. ONLY THE IMMEDIATE PARENT directory entry is emitted, not every ancestor. `/run` already exists in the image; emitting `run/` would rewrite an existing system directory's ownership for no gain. Emitting NEITHER also works (docker creates intermediates — measured), but the shape proven end to end is the one with the leaf's parent present, so that is what ships.
3. `uname`/`gname` are left EMPTY on purpose: a reader that resolves them prefers the NAME over the numeric id, and the measured read-back with both empty gave the intended 1000:1000.
4. `mtime` defaults to 0 so the same environment encodes to the same bytes. The delivery is read once at startup and removed with the deploy, so its timestamp carries nothing, and determinism lets an arm pin exact bytes.

THE UTF-8 TRAP IS CLOSED AND PROVEN CLOSED. The runner's stdin is a STRING and `runProcess` calls `child.stdin.write(stdin)`, which encodes UTF-8 — so the archive is emitted as a string whose non-payload bytes are all ASCII, and `size`/padding are computed with `Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8")`, never `String.length`. An arm proves the two actually differ for the case under test (`expect(multibyte.length).toBeLessThan(Buffer.byteLength(multibyte,"utf8"))`) before asserting the extraction round-trips, so it cannot pass on an all-ASCII input that would never have exercised the bug.
ONE DEFECT I FOUND AND FIXED IN MY OWN FIRST DRAFT: the header is laid out and checksummed in UTF-16 code units, which equal bytes only below U+0080, so a non-ASCII PATH would have shifted every field after `name` by a byte and produced an unparseable header. `entryNames` now refuses anything outside printable ASCII rather than encoding it.

REFUSALS, each a distinct stable code, because a truncated path delivers the environment somewhere the loader never reads — a candidate with no variables and no error: DEPLOY_ARCHIVE_PATH_TOO_LONG (past the 100-byte name field), DEPLOY_ARCHIVE_PATH_INVALID (not absolute, no parent, non-ASCII), DEPLOY_ARCHIVE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (past the 11-octal-digit size field).
